blocking_issues.title: T7 'awaiting_approval' is unimplementable inside the current WorkflowEngine under T7's own file-ownership limits
blocking_issues.detail: WorkflowEngine.run (latticeai/core/workflow_engine.py:224-321) is a synchronous run-to-completion loop with no suspension, no persisted node cursor, and no resume entry point; any exception a tool runner raises (e.g. an ApprovalRequired signal) is caught at lines 300-303, recorded as status='error', and the loop CONTINUES to the next node. Yet T7's ownership of workflow_engine.py is explicitly '(trigger vocabulary)' only. An implementer who honors the ownership contract cannot make a run pause at a non-auto-approve tool node and resume — the only in-contract options are fakes: pre-flight approval checks before the run starts, or marking a completed run 'awaiting_approval'. Resume semantics are also unspecified: re-entering run() from the top re-executes earlier side-effecting tool nodes, and the run 'context' dict holds arbitrary runner results that may not be JSON-serializable for a durable paused state.
blocking_issues.required_change: Expand T7 ownership to the full workflow_engine.py and specify the suspension model in the plan: engine raises/returns a PausedRun carrying the node cursor + JSON-serializable context snapshot; runner exceptions are partitioned (ApprovalRequired → pause, other → error-and-continue as today); resume re-enters at the paused node, never re-executes completed nodes; add an explicit test 'resume does not re-run prior tool nodes'.

blocking_issues.title: Async run engine spec is silent on the sync/async bridge, and the RealtimeBus it depends on is not thread-safe
blocking_issues.detail: T7 says 'background workers, cooperative cancellation, SSE progress over core/realtime.py'. But: (a) MultiAgentOrchestrator's role_runner contract is synchronous (multi_agent.py:414-427) while the real runtimes it must drive are async (core/agent.py awaits generate_as; llm_router.generate is async over a max_workers=1 ThreadPoolExecutor at llm_router.py:28) — calling asyncio.run() from a handler on the server loop fails, so runs must move to workers; (b) if workers are threads, RealtimeBus.publish does asyncio.Queue.put_nowait from a foreign thread (realtime.py:104) and the SSE stream() waiter (realtime.py:139) is not woken cross-thread — events will race or silently stall, producing a 'live progress' UI that lies; (c) core/realtime.py is in NO track's ownership list, so the implementer cannot fix the bus without violating the contract. The architecture's claim that 'the /agents events endpoint is already shaped for' SSE is also false — /agents/api/runs/{run_id}/events (api/agents.py:76-81) returns a JSON snapshot; the only SSE endpoint is /realtime/stream.
blocking_issues.required_change: Specify the concrete execution model in T7: asyncio tasks on the server loop as workers, sync tool/orchestrator work wrapped in asyncio.to_thread, and all bus publishes from non-loop threads routed through loop.call_soon_threadsafe; add core/realtime.py (thread-safe publish) to T7's ownership; correct the SSE claim and name the actual transport endpoint. Also state the honesty boundary that cooperative cancellation cannot interrupt an in-flight MLX generate() and that agent runs serialize with interactive chat on the single inference thread.

blocking_issues.title: Durable runs lie after a crash/restart: no startup reconciliation is specified
blocking_issues.detail: T7 promises 'persisted run lifecycle (queued → running → … cancelled)' executed by in-process workers, but the plan never says what happens to rows stuck in 'queued'/'running' when the uvicorn process dies mid-run (idle-unload, crash, user restart). Without a reconciliation pass, the UI will forever show phantom 'running' runs — exactly the class of fake state the ground rules forbid ('a capability that cannot complete must surface an explicit state'). The same applies to T7 interval/cron triggers: missed firings while the server was down need a defined policy or the scheduler silently skips work.
blocking_issues.required_change: Add to T7: on create_app startup, mark all non-terminal runs as 'interrupted' (with reason and timestamp) before workers start; define missed-trigger policy (skip with a recorded skip event, or fire-once catch-up); ship a test that restarts the engine with an in-flight run record and asserts the honest terminal state.

blocking_issues.title: T3 v2 flip will silently lose or merge edges: edges_v2 identity is keyed on legacy_type, which new canonical writes no longer mint
blocking_issues.detail: edges_v2 has UNIQUE(source, target, legacy_type) with legacy_type DEFAULT '' (kg_schema.py:333-347), deliberately keyed on the RAW legacy string. §3.1 simultaneously mandates that 'no new Korean free-string types are ever minted again' — so post-flip native writes have no legacy string. Two distinct canonical edges between the same pair (e.g. MENTIONS and CONTAINS, legacy_type='' for both) collide on the unique constraint: one upserts over the other, silent relationship loss in the authoritative store. Separately, the promised 'byte-equivalent reads before and after the flip' (test_kg_v2_read_equivalence) is only provable for pre-flip data; new rows definitionally project different (English-enum) legacy strings, so an implementer chasing literal byte-equivalence will be forced to keep minting Korean strings — the exact behavior the section bans.
blocking_issues.required_change: T3 must redefine post-flip edge identity (UNIQUE on (source, target, type) for canonical rows, with the legacy_type constraint preserved only for migrated rows, or a recreated table with a composite key) including the SQLite constraint-migration steps; and scope the equivalence test contract explicitly to data existing before the flip, with a separate projection-correctness test for new canonical writes.

blocking_issues.title: Backend tracks promise UI surfaces that no track owns — Brain Network, approvals, and context-trace will ship invisible or invented
blocking_issues.detail: T7 says pending approvals are 'surfaced through the API/UI'; T8 says the device fingerprint is 'surfaced in UI/API' and requires a 'deliberate pairing step'; T5 promises a per-section context trace 'exposed to the UI'; T4 exposes a provenance-coverage metric. T9 owns all of static/v3/** but its enumerated deliverables (IA regroup, graph canvas port, legacy deletion, vendoring, i18n, build/lint) contain NONE of these views, and the plan declares T9 'independent of T3-T8 except for new API names' and parallel-safe — meaning T9 can complete before the T7/T8 APIs even exist. The likely outcomes are exactly the fake-functionality failure modes the charter bans: pairing/approval views wired to endpoints that don't exist yet, or real backend capabilities (Brain Network v1, per-tool approval, 'why is this in my context') shipping with no operable surface while docs claim them as product features.
blocking_issues.required_change: Either (a) add an enumerated T9 deliverable list for the new surfaces — runs/approvals inbox (Act), peer registry + pairing + fingerprint (System), context-trace panel (Ask), provenance coverage (Brain) — with an explicit dependency on T7/T8 API contracts and matching Playwright tests; or (b) declare these capabilities API-only for v4.0.0 in both docs and FEATURE_STATUS.md so the absence is a labeled state, not an omission discovered at RC.

non_blocking_issues.title: 'Disjoint file ownership' is factually false; sequencing is the only real protection
non_blocking_issues.detail: api/chat.py is owned by T1 (context filter), T2 (telegram import), and T5 (context build); server_app.py by T2 (assembly) and T4 (save_to_history call); api/workspace.py by T1 (authz) and T9 (onboarding route); brain/store.py by T3 (creation) and T6 (scoping joins). The 'tracks can't conflict' claim only holds if tracks run strictly sequentially — but T9 is explicitly advertised as parallel-safe while sharing api/workspace.py with T1's authz fixes. The plan should replace the disjointness claim with an ordered-handoff rule per shared file.

non_blocking_issues.title: T2's create_app acceptance test is trivially gameable
non_blocking_issues.detail: The stated gate — 'factory produces a working app (TestClient)' — passes with def create_app(cfg): import latticeai.server_app; return server_app.app, leaving every import-time singleton and MLX side effect intact. server_app.py builds CONFIG/WORKSPACE_OS/KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH/CHAT_SERVICE and ~27 routers at import with 25-30-kwarg closures; 'keep module-level names as thin accessors' via module __getattr__ silently reintroduces construction-on-first-touch. Add a non-gameable check: import the module in a subprocess and assert no model init / no KG store construction occurred (e.g., via an env flag or constructor counter).

non_blocking_issues.title: T7 LLM role-runner failure handling is unspecified — the fabrication pathway can reopen under a new name
non_blocking_issues.detail: Small local MLX models will frequently emit unparseable plan/critique JSON. The spec defines only mode:'llm' vs mode:'simulation' but not what happens when generation succeeds and parsing fails, or when the model is idle-unloaded mid-run (server_app.py:1036 unload loop). An implementer under pressure will silently fall back to the canned deterministic plan while keeping mode:'llm' — fabricated provenance with better labeling. Define: parse failure → run fails or mode:'llm_degraded' persisted per-step; mode is recorded per role invocation, not once per run.

non_blocking_issues.title: T4's chat-history retirement reaches outside its declared ownership
non_blocking_issues.detail: Retiring chat_history.json touches get_history(), ChatService wiring (server_app.py:698-700), and the /history read endpoints — but T4 owns server_app.py for the 'save_to_history call only'. Similarly the deliverable 'chat context no longer reads the vault' is only achievable in-contract by re-implementing PReinforceGardener.get_relevant_context as a brain query inside p_reinforce.py (T4-owned), since the call site api/chat.py:368 belongs to T5/T1; the plan should state this explicitly so the implementer doesn't either stall or edit chat.py.

non_blocking_issues.title: i18n (en/ko) across 22 SPA views has no coverage gate — the classic quietly-skipped deliverable
non_blocking_issues.detail: T9 item 5 says 'i18n dictionary (en/ko)' with no acceptance criterion in the test list. Externalizing every string from ~22 views is large, mechanical, and unverifiable as specified — the predictable outcome is a dictionary with 30 keys and hardcoded English everywhere else, claimed complete. Extend lint_v3.mjs with an untranslated-literal rule or a string-coverage assertion, or descope i18n to named views honestly.

non_blocking_issues.title: Legacy-page deletion is gated on redirects, not feature parity
non_blocking_issues.detail: T9's tests prove routes redirect, not that the v3 chat view preserves legacy chat capabilities (doc-gen sessions via _doc_gen_sessions in api/chat.py, image attach, auto file-path injection rendering). Capability preservation is a charter constraint; add a parity checklist per deleted page against FEATURE_STATUS.md before the deletion commit.

non_blocking_issues.title: Brain Network v1 transport security is underspecified: peer authentication and replay
non_blocking_issues.detail: T8 defines signature verification of bundles against the paired key, but not how the receiving HTTP endpoint authenticates the push itself (session auth won't exist for peers), nor replay protection (re-pushing an old validly-signed bundle), nor authorization on pull ('which peer may pull which workspace'). Without this, the implementer either opens an unauthenticated import endpoint or invents an ad-hoc scheme at 2am. Specify: request signed over body+timestamp+nonce with the device key, paired-key check before processing, and a per-peer workspace allowlist.

non_blocking_issues.title: FTS5 needs the same capability-honest fallback discipline as sqlite-vec
non_blocking_issues.detail: FTS5 is present in the dev venv (verified) and in most CPython builds, but the plan mandates the honest-fallback pattern only for sqlite-vec. A user's Python built without FTS5 would crash the new query path. One line in T3: probe FTS5 at store init, fall back to the LIKE path, and report the grade in capabilities — same pattern already used for embeddings.

non_blocking_issues.title: ContextAssembler 'token-budgeted' has no tokenizer specified
non_blocking_issues.detail: T5 promises token budgets but the stack has no model-agnostic tokenizer dependency; the implementer will count characters and call it tokens. Acceptable — but specify the approximation (e.g., chars/4 heuristic or the loaded model's tokenizer when available) and label the budget unit in the trace, so the 'why is this in context' explanation doesn't claim precision it lacks.

non_blocking_issues.title: Architecture doc minor inaccuracy: /agents events endpoint shape
non_blocking_issues.detail: V4_BRAIN_ARCHITECTURE.md §6 says the /agents events endpoint is 'already shaped for' SSE streaming; api/agents.py:76-81 returns a JSON snapshot via runtime.events(). The real SSE precedent is /realtime/stream (api/realtime.py:46-63). Cosmetic, but this doc is the contract implementers code against — fix the reference.

non_blocking_issues.title: T3 'mechanical decomposition' has no definition of done
non_blocking_issues.detail: Splitting the 4,633-line KnowledgeGraphStore 'along its existing seams' with only 'full suite green' as the gate permits a pure mixin-shuffle (same god-object, five files). If that is acceptable as step one, say so; otherwise name the intended module boundaries' public APIs (what store.py exposes vs extraction.py) so the reviewer agent has something objective to check.

blocking_issues.title: T3 flip has no real rollback: any v4→v3.6 downgrade silently destroys the write-mastered brain
blocking_issues.detail: v3.6's init path treats v2 as a disposable projection: knowledge_graph.py:1042-1043 executes 'DROP TABLE IF EXISTS edges_v2/nodes_v2' on a stale version stamp, and _backfill_v2_on (knowledge_graph.py:1101-1102) runs 'DELETE FROM edges_v2; DELETE FROM nodes_v2' then re-projects from legacy tables. After the T3 flip, nodes_v2/edges_v2 are the master and hold data the legacy projection cannot represent (owner_id, workspace_id, visibility, evidence, confidence, observed_at occurrence records, superseded_by). If a user downgrades (pip install of v3.6, revert after RC, restoring an old environment), the old code wipes the master and regenerates a lossy projection — and a subsequent re-upgrade's 'one-time' migrator, if keyed on a surviving graph_meta stamp, will not re-run, permanently corrupting the brain. The risk register's claim that the flip 'lands as its own commit (revertable in isolation)' covers code only, not released-binary downgrade. The plan's reversibility story (legacy tables as regenerated read-compat projection) does not address this.
blocking_issues.required_change: Add an explicit downgrade guard to the T3 design: bump a DB format marker (e.g., PRAGMA user_version or kg_meta key) that the v4 code sets at flip time, document that v3.6 will destroy v2 data on contact, retain the automatic pre-flip VACUUM INTO backup with a documented restore runbook, and make the migrator re-entrant keyed on actual data-state inspection (e.g., detect legacy-master vs v2-master by content/markers), not a one-time stamp.

blocking_issues.title: edges_v2 UNIQUE(source, target, legacy_type) corrupts data under native canonical writes
blocking_issues.detail: kg_schema.py:335-345: edges_v2 has 'legacy_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT \'\'' and 'UNIQUE(source, target, legacy_type)' — edge identity deliberately follows the raw legacy string. T3 mandates that all new writes use canonical enums and 'no new Korean free-string types are ever minted again', i.e., legacy_type='' for every v4-native edge. Then any two semantically distinct canonical edges between the same node pair (e.g., MENTIONS and DECIDED_BY) collide on UNIQUE(source, target, '') — inserts fail or upserts silently merge/overwrite distinct relations (weight/confidence/evidence of one relation clobbering another). SQLite cannot alter a table-level UNIQUE constraint; the fix requires an edges_v2 table rebuild, which contradicts the plan's 'additive, reversible' migration framing and is nowhere mentioned in T3.
blocking_issues.required_change: T3 must specify the new edge identity key for write-mastering (e.g., UNIQUE(source, target, type, legacy_type) or a normalized occurrence model) and an explicit edges_v2 table-rebuild migration step (create-new → copy → swap inside one transaction, covered by the pre-migration backup), plus tests proving two canonical-typed edges between the same pair coexist.

blocking_issues.title: T4 conversation cutover imports nothing — existing chat history is lost at upgrade
blocking_issues.detail: chat_history.json (written by save_to_history, latticeai/server_app.py:623-668, capped at history[-50:]) is the only raw conversation record and feeds the v3 chat UI's conversation list (static/v3/js/views/chat.js loadConversations → api.chatHistory()). T4 says the new conversations/messages store starts as the source of truth and 'chat_history.json retired to render-cache or removed' — no one-time import of the existing file is specified, so users' visible chat history vanishes on upgrade, violating 'user data must survive'. Additionally, legacy entries may lack user_email and conversation_id (telegram/anonymous sources), so a 'per-user, per-conversation' store needs a documented attribution rule for them, and no track owns updating chat.js to a new conversations API if the /chat/history response shape changes (T4 owns no static files; T9's item list doesn't include the chat view).
blocking_issues.required_change: Add to T4: a one-time idempotent import of chat_history.json into the conversations store with an explicit attribution rule for messages lacking user_email/conversation_id (e.g., a designated 'legacy' conversation per source), preservation of the /chat/history API response contract (or add the chat-view rewire to T9's owned scope), and a durability test that pre-upgrade messages remain visible post-cutover.

blocking_issues.title: User-UUID migration leaves the brain and workspace records keyed on mutable emails; users.json rewrite is non-atomic
blocking_issues.detail: Track ordering: T3 populates nodes_v2.owner_id/created_by at every write site before UUIDs exist (T6), so those values will be emails; workspace_os.py has ~30 email-keyed sites (memories, memberships, audit, run records), and users.json is an email-keyed dict (server_app.py:458-466). T6 item 2 only re-keys 'sessions/memberships' on UUIDs — no step rewrites nodes_v2.owner_id/created_by, workspace memories' owners, or audit entries from email→UUID. Once scoped reads filter by UUID and email becomes 'a mutable attribute', email-owned rows stop matching their owner: private knowledge becomes invisible (perceived data loss) or is mis-classified under the NULL/legacy-global compatibility rule (privacy regression). Also, save_users (server_app.py:464-466) writes users.json via a plain open('w')+json.dump — no tmp+os.replace — so the UUID migration rewriting every account through it can corrupt the entire user store on a crash; and load_users/save_users live in server_app.py, which T6 does not own (T2 owns it 'assembly only'), an ownership gap for the migration code.
blocking_issues.required_change: T6 must include: (a) a single identity-value migration that rewrites owner/created_by/member/audit keys from email→UUID across users.json, workspace_os state, sessions, AND nodes_v2/edges_v2 (or T3 must write a stable placeholder resolved by T6); (b) atomic tmp+rename writes and a timestamped pre-migration copy of users.json/workspace_os.json; (c) explicit ownership of server_app.py's user-store functions assigned to T6 (or the store moved into T6-owned modules first).

blocking_issues.title: T9 legacy deletion removes org-workspace, snapshot/time-machine, activity, and profile capabilities that have NO /app equivalent today
blocking_issues.detail: Verified by grep: static/v3/js/views/ contains zero references to 'snapshots', 'time-machine', or workspace activation/orgs management (only an unused api.js createOrg helper, static/v3/js/core/api.js:281). Legacy static/workspace.html + static/scripts/workspace.js (948 lines) is the ONLY UI for: org workspace create/activate/members (/workspace/orgs, /workspace/activate), snapshots + compare + time-machine (/workspace/snapshots, /workspace/time-machine), workspace memories admin, indexing dashboard pause/resume (/workspace/indexing), and the relationship explorer. static/activity.html (presence + realtime stream feed) and account profile editing (/account/profile in static/scripts/account.js) likewise have no v3 view. T9 deletes these pages and 308-redirects to '/app equivalents' that do not exist, and T9's six work items add none of them (only IA regroup, graph canvas port, login rebuild, vendoring, build/lint/i18n, tests). This degrades/hides the preserved capabilities 'personal + organization workspace' and 'backup/restore' (workspace snapshots/time-machine are the user-facing restore-point surface), and T6's new invitation flow ships with no UI at all.
blocking_issues.required_change: Extend T9's contract with explicit new /app views before any deletion commit: Workspace/Org management (orgs, members, invitations, activation), Snapshots/Time-Machine (list/create/compare/restore), activity feed, and account profile editing — or stage deletion per-page, deleting only pages whose equivalent view exists and passes Playwright coverage; the redirect map must be capability-complete, not URL-complete.

blocking_issues.title: New durable stores (conversations, workspace state) fall outside backup/restore and export/import unless explicitly co-located
blocking_issues.detail: kg_portability.backup() (latticeai/services/kg_portability.py:96-105) snapshots only the KG SQLite DB via KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH.backup_database (VACUUM INTO, knowledge_graph.py:3349-3367); export/import likewise covers graph content only. The architecture places conversations (§3.3) and transactional workspace state (§5) in 'the brain DB family' — ambiguous between 'same SQLite file' and 'sibling DB files'. If they are separate files: (a) the preserved backup/restore capability silently stops covering the user's conversations and workspace state; (b) restoring a KG backup desynchronizes the graph from the conversation/workspace stores (episodic nodes referencing missing messages, provenance pointing at absent records); (c) the T6 ground-rule promise that 'every schema migration is preceded by an automatic backup (existing kg_portability machinery)' is false for the JSON→SQLite and UUID migrations, since that machinery cannot back up workspace_os.json or users.json. T8 touches kg_portability only for signing.
blocking_issues.required_change: Pin the decision in T4/T6: either all new tables live in the same backed-up SQLite file (and the restore path is tested to carry them), or kg_portability backup/restore/export manifests are extended to enumerate every brain store atomically; separately, mandate migration-time timestamped copies of workspace_os.json and users.json since kg_portability cannot cover them.

blocking_issues.title: Approval gate, simulation labeling, and context-trace surfaces are promised but no track owns their UI — workflows regress from 'completes' to 'hangs'
blocking_issues.detail: T7 makes approve() stop auto-approving and pauses non-auto-approve tool nodes into awaiting_approval; architecture §6 promises the pending decision is 'surfaced through the API/UI', T5 promises a per-section 'why is this in context?' trace exposed to the UI, T8 promises the device fingerprint 'surfaced in UI/API', and T1/T7 add mode:'simulation' badges-worth of state. T9's six items include none of these surfaces, and grep shows no v3 view has any run-approval affordance (approve appears only in files/tools/planning contexts). Concretely: a v3.6 workflow containing a non-auto-approve tool completes today (dishonestly, via {recorded:true}); under v4 it pauses forever with no UI to approve/resume — breaking the preserved 'workflows' capability and the /workflows UX contract. Existing tests also encode the old contract: tests/unit/test_agent_platform_maturity.py:94 asserts run.status=='ok' for agent/plugin workflow outputs, which T7's 'execute or honestly refuse' will flip; and T1 removes run graph_node_id stamping (workspace_os.py:1331-1342) for simulated runs, changing the run-record shape consumers see.
blocking_issues.required_change: Assign the approval inbox/resume UI, run-mode (simulation/llm) badge, trigger management, and context-trace panel to a named track (T9 scope addition with file ownership), with Playwright coverage for pause→approve→resume; enumerate the run-record contract changes (mode field, conditional graph_node_id, awaiting_approval status) and the specific legacy tests (test_agent_platform_maturity, test_v32_platform, test_multi_agent) to be rewritten rather than discovered broken mid-track.

blocking_issues.title: Garden absorption as one-time import breaks the live Obsidian-vault capability despite the 'no capability removed' claim
blocking_issues.detail: p_reinforce.py:15-19 resolves the vault from LATTICEAI_OBSIDIAN_VAULT_DIR — the vault is explicitly designed to BE the user's Obsidian vault, and get_relevant_context (p_reinforce.py:130-148) rglobs live files at query time, so notes the user adds/edits in Obsidian are immediately retrievable in chat today. T4 replaces this with a one-time idempotent import after which 'the gardener stops being a parallel store': (a) post-import Obsidian edits and new notes never enter the brain — silent capability loss for vault users; (b) /garden POST currently produces classified markdown files in the vault (process(), p_reinforce.py:85-104) — re-implementing it as brain-only writes removes the Obsidian-artifact output. The classification taxonomy itself survives as an enricher, but the architecture's claim 'No capability is removed — notes, classification, and relevant context in chat survive' (§4.2) is false for the live-vault dimension. (Baseline note for honest comparison: /garden/tree already 500s — latticeai/api/garden.py:33 calls gardener.get_tree(), which does not exist on PReinforceGardener.)
blocking_issues.required_change: Replace 'one-time import' with continuous ingestion: register the vault directory as a watched knowledge source via the existing discovery/watch machinery (knowledge_sources + watcher) so post-import Obsidian edits keep flowing into the brain, and make an explicit recorded decision on the markdown write-out (keep dual-artifact note writing into the vault, or formally deprecate it in FEATURE_STATUS with user-visible labeling — not silently).

non_blocking_issues.title: FTS5 replacing LIKE risks Korean-recall regression
non_blocking_issues.detail: LIKE '%q%' matches substrings inside agglutinated Korean tokens (query '프로젝트' matches '프로젝트를'); FTS5's default unicode61 tokenizer indexes whole tokens and will not, and the graph is heavily Korean (legacy free-string types like '업로드함', ko content). T3's 'FTS5 parity tests' must include Korean morphology/particle cases; consider the trigram tokenizer or retaining a LIKE fallback for short CJK queries, or 'search' (a preserved capability) quietly degrades for the product's primary language.

non_blocking_issues.title: Migrated legacy rows: visibility DEFAULT 'private' contradicts the documented NULL=legacy-global rule
non_blocking_issues.detail: nodes_v2.visibility is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'private' (kg_schema.py:322). The architecture says pre-v4 rows are 'legacy-global, readable by all members of the machine'. If the T3 migrator leaves visibility='private' with owner_id NULL, T6's scoped reads will either hide legacy rows from everyone (perceived data loss) or need a special case that contradicts the column value. The migrator must set an explicit visibility (e.g., 'legacy-global') and tests must cover legacy-row readability after scoping lands.

non_blocking_issues.title: Garden import scope/ownership is undecided
non_blocking_issues.detail: Today the vault context is injected into every user's chat (api/chat.py:368) — effectively machine-global. T4 must decide what workspace_id/owner imported vault notes get: NULL/legacy-global preserves today's behavior but institutionalizes personal notes being readable by all machine users post-T6; importing into one user's personal brain changes other users' chat context. Either is defensible; the plan should state it and label the privacy consequence in docs.

non_blocking_issues.title: T6 JSON→SQLite rollback is a silent one-way door
non_blocking_issues.detail: workspace_os.json and users.json are left in place per the absorption rule, but after the cutover they are frozen snapshots; reverting to v3.6 resumes from stale state and silently loses everything written to the SQLite stores since migration. Same applies to the conversation store. Document the one-way door explicitly in release notes and take timestamped copies of the JSON files at migration time so the divergence point is at least recoverable.

non_blocking_issues.title: 'Byte-equivalent reads before and after the flip' is only achievable for pre-existing rows
non_blocking_issues.detail: Post-flip native rows carry canonical enum types with empty legacy_type; the inverse projection will surface English enum strings in the legacy tables, so legacy-surface reads of NEW data cannot be byte-equivalent to what the Korean-string write paths would have produced. The equivalence suite claim should be scoped honestly to migrated data, and the deprecation-window rendering difference noted (legacy /graph UI labels change for new nodes).

non_blocking_issues.title: kg_portability backup destination lives on the same disk as the DB
non_blocking_issues.detail: Pre-migration backups land in the exports dir inside the same data directory (kg_portability.py:99). Fine for migration-bug rollback, useless for disk failure; for the v4 migration specifically, consider honoring a user-configurable backup destination and printing the backup path prominently in the migration log so users can copy it off-disk before upgrading.

non_blocking_issues.title: T1 run-record shape change should be versioned, not just made
non_blocking_issues.detail: Dropping graph_node_id stamping for simulated runs (workspace_os.py:1331-1342) and adding the mode field changes a persisted record shape that the relationship explorer and tests (test_workspace_os.py asserts graph_node_id formats elsewhere) read. Add a record-shape note to the run schema and grep-driven consumer audit to T1's checklist so the change is deliberate everywhere it lands.

blocking_issues.title: T2 deletes knowledge_graph_api.py based on a false audit fact, breaking the KG-first UI mid-release
blocking_issues.detail: Plan T2.4 calls knowledge_graph_api.py a dead module and says to 'fold its one endpoint into api/local_files.py'. The module actually defines ~10 live routes (/graph page, /knowledge-graph page, and /knowledge-graph/{stats,schema,graph,documents,search,context,neighbors,ingest}) wired through latticeai/api/local_files.py:17,208. The v3 SPA's primary Knowledge Graph and Files views consume them directly (static/v3/js/core/api.js:100,129,137,449-451). Executing T2 as written breaks the preserved capabilities 'KG first-class' and 'graph visualization' for all of T3-T8, and T9's own task list ('knowledge_graph_api-served /graph route relocation') then references a module deleted seven tracks earlier — a direct T2/T9 contradiction. The error propagated from docs/v4-audit/v4_audit_backend-architecture.json ('vestigial one-endpoint router') into both V4_BRAIN_ARCHITECTURE.md §9 and the plan.
blocking_issues.required_change: Correct the inventory in both docs: knowledge_graph_api.py is a live router. Assign one owner for its migration: data endpoints (/knowledge-graph/*) move into latticeai/api/ (T2 or T3) with endpoint-parity tests proving the v3 SPA contract (stats/graph/documents/search/context/neighbors/ingest) is unchanged; the legacy /graph and /knowledge-graph page routes move to T9's redirect work. Remove the module from T2's 'dead modules' deletion list.

blocking_issues.title: Architecture promises work that no track owns (llm_router/mcp_registry move, local_knowledge_api.py, env-prefix canonicalization, CLI alias, wizard embedder provisioning)
blocking_issues.detail: V4_BRAIN_ARCHITECTURE.md §9 states 'llm_router.py, mcp_registry.py, kg_schema.py move under latticeai/' — only kg_schema is assigned (T3). No track owns llm_router.py or mcp_registry.py, and their importers (latticeai/api/models.py, latticeai/services/model_runtime.py) appear in no ownership list anywhere in the plan. local_knowledge_api.py (345 lines, 7 routes incl. /knowledge-graph/local/* folder-watch used by the my-computer view; imported at latticeai/server_app.py:37 and api/local_files.py:18) is mentioned in neither document despite §9's claim that 'the dependency inversion ends'. §2's LATTICEAI_*/LATTICE_* env alias scheme and the ltcai/LTCAI CLI alias have no owning track (latticeai/core/config.py is in no ownership list; T10 owns package.json 'files list' only). §3.1/§11 say the real-embedder wizard provisioning 'capability ships', but T2 owns only the setup.py→setup_wizard.py rename and T3 owns neither setup_wizard.py nor api/setup.py. Under the program's own rules, unowned promises get either silently cut (violates the no-deferral directive) or hacked in via ownership violations.
blocking_issues.required_change: Amend the plan so every §2/§3.1/§9/§11 promise has an owning track: add llm_router/mcp_registry relocation (plus api/models.py and services/model_runtime.py import updates) to T2 or a T2b; add local_knowledge_api.py disposition (absorb into latticeai/brain/discovery.py per the T3 seam, or latticeai/api/) explicitly; assign env-alias work on core/config.py and CLI bin aliases to a named track; grant the wizard embedder-provisioning flow to a track that owns setup_wizard.py/api/setup.py.

blocking_issues.title: File-ownership 'disjoint' guarantee is false; at least three tracks must edit files they do not own
blocking_issues.detail: The plan asserts 'file ownership is disjoint per track so tracks can't conflict', but: (a) T3.5 wires graph_curator into services/ingestion.py, which T4 owns and rewrites one track later; (b) T4's test 'chat context no longer reads the vault' requires removing the gardener call at latticeai/api/chat.py:368 (chat.py is owned by T1 'context filter only', T2 'telegram import only', and T5 'context build' — never T4) and disabling the gardener writer wired at server_app.py:987/1451/1543, outside T4's 'save_to_history call only' slice; (c) T8's per-workspace export and origin-device import provenance must modify export_graph_data/import_graph_data, which live in the store (kg_portability.py:63,87 merely delegates) — brain/store.py is T3/T6-owned, not T8's. Additionally chat.py, workspace.py, workspace_os.py, multi_agent.py, agent_runtime.py, server_app.py, brain/store.py, and static/v3/** each have 2-3 owning tracks, which only works if execution is strictly serial.
blocking_issues.required_change: Restate the rule as sequential sub-file ownership and make each grant explicit: move the graph_curator wire-or-delete decision from T3 to T4; move 'chat context stops reading the vault' (api/chat.py:368) and its test from T4 to T5, leaving T4 only the import + /garden re-pointing + gardener-writer deactivation (with an explicit server_app.py gardener-wiring grant); grant T8 the store's export_graph_data/import_graph_data functions (or have T6 land scope-filtered export and provenance-stamped import hooks that T8 consumes).

blocking_issues.title: Signed-bundle import verification has no stated policy for pre-v4 unsigned bundles and backups
blocking_issues.detail: V4_BRAIN_ARCHITECTURE.md §7 says 'imports verify and record origin provenance' and T8's tests cover 'tampered bundle rejected, unpaired peer rejected' — but every existing v3.6.0 export and backup archive is unsigned (kg_portability today produces sha256-manifested, unsigned artifacts; restore() at kg_portability.py:122 verifies hashes only). If verification is mandatory on import, users' existing backups stop restoring — breaking the preserved backup/restore capability and the 'user data must survive' constraint. Neither document states the policy, and no T8 test asserts legacy-bundle acceptance.
blocking_issues.required_change: Add an explicit policy to §7 and T8: local file imports of unsigned (pre-v4) bundles are accepted and recorded with provenance origin='unsigned-legacy'; signatures are mandatory only for Brain Network peer exchange. Add a T8 test: a v3.6.0-format unsigned export imports successfully and a restore of a pre-v4 backup archive succeeds.

blocking_issues.title: T5/T7/T8 architecture-promised UI surfaces are assigned to no track, while T9 is declared parallel-safe before their APIs exist
blocking_issues.detail: The architecture promises user-facing surfaces: per-section context trace ('why is this in my context?' — §3.4, T5.2 'exposed to the UI'), awaiting_approval pending-decision UI (§6 'surfaces the pending decision through the API/UI'), run progress/cancellation over SSE, trigger configuration, and device fingerprint + peer pairing UI (T8.1 'surfaced in UI/API'). T9's task list (items 1-6: IA regroup, canvas port, legacy deletion, vendoring, build/lint/i18n, tests) contains none of these, and T9 is declared 'parallel-safe with T3-T8 after T1' — i.e., it may complete before the T5/T7/T8 APIs it would need even exist. The plan also never enumerates the 'new API names' T9 is excepted on (/api/brain/provenance/coverage from T4, context trace from T5, run lifecycle from T7, network API from T8). Unowned UI for shipped backend capability invites exactly the 'UI illusion' / silent-cut failure modes the program forbids.
blocking_issues.required_change: Enumerate the new API contracts (names + shapes) in the plan as a shared appendix, and add explicit T9 tasks (or a T9b phase sequenced after T7/T8) for: context-trace display, approval-decision UI, run progress/cancel UI, trigger configuration, and network pairing/fingerprint UI. Drop or qualify the 'parallel-safe' claim to cover only T9 items 2-5.

blocking_issues.title: T3's v2 write-mastering claims column population it cannot deliver at T3 time
blocking_issues.detail: T3.2 says 'Canonical enums at every write site; populate owner/workspace/visibility/created_by/evidence', but the write sites are in files T3 does not own (server_app.py and upload_service/mcp are T4's; chat is T5's), and workspace scope resolution on reads/writes is T6 work. As sequenced, at T3-close most writes still arrive without owner/workspace context, so the columns 'that justify v2's existence' (arch §3.1) remain largely NULL — meaning the architecture's headline claim for the flip is only actually true after T6, with no checkpoint verifying it.
blocking_issues.required_change: Restate T3.2 as normalization and column plumbing at the store boundary: brain/store.py write APIs accept owner_id/workspace_id/visibility parameters (defaulting to legacy-global NULL per §5), with enum normalization enforced inside the store so no caller can mint free-string types. State explicitly that T4 (ingestion callers) and T6 (scope resolution) progressively supply the values, and add a T6-close acceptance check: percentage of post-T4 writes carrying owner/workspace is reported via the provenance coverage endpoint and asserted in tests.

non_blocking_issues.title: T3's four-module brain/ decomposition leaves store.py as a new ~3,000-line monolith
non_blocking_issues.detail: KnowledgeGraphStore's real method clusters are: store/v2 projection (knowledge_graph.py:811-1410), local discovery (1411-2596), ingest (2597-3096), provenance (3097-3232), portability export/import/backup (3233-3368), document structure (3369-3567), query/graph/search/traverse (3568-4054), vector index (4055-4362), maintenance/stats (4363-4633). T3 names only store/extraction/documents/discovery, implicitly dumping ingest+provenance+query+vector+portability (~2,500-3,000 lines) into store.py. The seams for provenance.py, query.py (or retrieval.py), and vectors.py exist in the class and match the architecture's own §3.x system boundaries; either name them or state explicitly that store.py retains them and why.

non_blocking_issues.title: T1's hybrid-search.js honesty fix may not reach the shipped bundle until T9
non_blocking_issues.detail: Hashed build artifacts (e.g., static/v3/js/views/hybrid-search.b22b97e0.js) are committed alongside sources, and the build scripts (scripts/build_v3_assets.mjs) are T9-owned. If the SPA loads hashed artifacts, T1's removal of the fabricated fusion meters in hybrid-search.js is invisible until T9 rebuilds — eight tracks during which the known-fake UI still ships. T1 should regenerate the affected artifact or be granted a build-script run.

non_blocking_issues.title: Ingestion coverage arithmetic is internally inconsistent (1/4 -> 4/4 vs five listed sources)
non_blocking_issues.detail: Arch §4.1 headlines 'Coverage goes 1/4 -> 4/4' but lists chat messages, document uploads, MCP messages, and workspace events as the new paths — with browser already covered, that is five sources. The audit's four paths are browser/chat/uploads/MCP; workspace events are a new source whose producer (core/workspace_os.py) is owned by T1/T6, not T4. Clarify whether workspace events count in the coverage metric and who wires their emission into the pipeline.

non_blocking_issues.title: T6's 'invitations API' names no file
non_blocking_issues.detail: Every other ownership entry is a concrete path; 'invitations API' is the only unanchored item in T6's list. Name the router file (new latticeai/api/invitations.py or a section of api/workspace.py — the latter would add a fourth owner to an already three-owner file).

non_blocking_issues.title: Recovery file's superseded C-queue still contains decisions that contradict the plan
non_blocking_issues.detail: docs/V4_DIGITAL_BRAIN_RECOVERY.md §7 retains the provisional C1-C9 queue (e.g., C1 includes session-token hashing/PKCE, which the plan moved to T6.5). It is marked SUPERSEDED, but the file is the designated cross-session recovery artifact; a resumed session skimming §7 could execute the stale ordering. Consider trimming §7 to a one-line pointer at the next update.

non_blocking_issues.title: Scope is achievable only as a strictly serial pipeline — say so
non_blocking_issues.detail: Given the multi-owner files (chat.py x3, server_app.py x2, workspace_os.py x2, brain/store.py x2, static/v3 x2) and the dependency spine T1->T2->T3->T4->T5->T6->T7/T8->T9->T10, the release is coherent only if tracks run strictly in sequence with the recovery-file checkpoint between each. That is consistent with the no-deferral directive (nothing needs cutting), but the plan's parallelism language ('tracks can't conflict', 'T9 parallel-safe') invites the one execution mode that does conflict. State serial execution as the model; it is already what the per-track commit/review loop implies.
